key_insight: A self-supervised CT foundation model, CIPHER, can predict which lung cancer patients are at higher risk of immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced pneumonitis before treatment starts.
clinical_relevance: If validated further, this approach could help clinicians identify higher-risk patients early for closer monitoring and faster intervention during immunotherapy.
method: Pretrained on 590,284 CT slices from 2,500 NSCLC patients using contrastive learning plus a transformer-based masked autoencoder.
Fine-tuned on an internal immunotherapy cohort and evaluated on held-out internal and independent external validation cohorts.
Benchmarked against clinical, radiomics, and ensemble comparator models for head-to-head performance.
evidence_signal: CIPHER achieved AUCs of 0.77-0.85 internally, AUC 0.83 in benchmarking, and AUC 0.83 with 81.7% balanced accuracy in external validation, outperforming radiomics.
watch_item: The model was trained and tested in retrospective cohorts, so broader multi-center prospective validation and workflow integration are still needed before routine use.
paper_title: CT-Based Deep Foundation Model for Predicting Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-Induced Pneumonitis Risk in Lung Cancer
